metadata.source: Arabic Language Mastery SKILL.md - Cultural Context Engine

essential_expressions.usage: Before starting any task (eating, entering, traveling)
Expressing gratitude, after 'how are you?', after finishing tasks
Whenever discussing future plans or intentions
essential_expressions.note: Omitting this when discussing future plans can be considered presumptuous

essential_expressions.usage: Expressing admiration, protecting against evil eye
essential_expressions.response: الله يبارك فيك (Allāh yubārik fīk) - God bless you

essential_expressions.literal: may God reward you with goodness

essential_expressions.usage: Expressing regret, shock, or when correcting oneself
Expressing amazement or when witnessing something remarkable

greetings_sequence.description: Proper greeting protocol in Arabic culture

steps.note: May continue for several exchanges in formal settings

greetings_sequence.cultural_note: Rushing through greetings is considered rude. Invest time in proper hellos.

coffee_tea_protocol.accepting: Accept at least one cup (refusing all can be offensive)
coffee_tea_protocol.declining: Shake the cup gently side-to-side to indicate 'no more'

food_customs.insistence: Host will insist multiple times - refusing once is not final
food_customs.eating: Use right hand only for eating
food_customs.finishing: Leave small amount on plate to show satisfaction

respectful_terms.usage: Respectful for elderly who completed Hajj

level_1_very_formal.name: Very Formal MSA
level_1_very_formal.context: Official documents, religious sermons, academic papers, diplomatic communications
level_1_very_formal.example: نحن نتشرف بدعوتكم لحضور الحفل الختامي

level_2_formal.name: Formal Educated Spoken
level_2_formal.context: Business meetings, university lectures, professional emails, news broadcasts

level_3_semi_formal.name: Semi-Formal Polite Dialect
level_3_semi_formal.context: Casual business, speaking with strangers, shop transactions

level_4_informal.name: Informal Casual Dialect
level_4_informal.context: Friends, family, social media casual posts
level_4_informal.example: شو عم تعمل؟ (shū ʿam taʿmil - Levantine)

level_5_very_informal.name: Very Informal Slang
level_5_very_informal.context: Close friends, youth culture, internet memes

general_rules.physical_contact: Avoid handshakes with opposite gender unless initiated
general_rules.eye_contact: Moderate - too much can be considered aggressive/flirtatious

business_contexts.meetings: Wait for woman to extend hand first
business_contexts.seating: May be gender-segregated in very conservative settings

etiquette.giving: Use right hand or both hands
etiquette.receiving: Accept with right hand, express gratitude
etiquette.opening: May not open immediately in front of giver (varies by region)
